bug_description.normalized: The staged TrueType witness contains a Graphite `Silf` table at file offset 76404 with length 92040. Its first eight table bytes are version `0x00050001` and compression header `0x0807c424`, so `ots::OpenTypeSILF::Parse` takes the outer version-5 LZ4 path and derives `decompressed_size = 508964`. Vulnerable `src/silf.cc` then allocates `decompressed` with `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]`, leaving the whole heap output buffer uninitialized, and calls `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial`. In the saved Stage 01 run, that call returns the full `decompressed_size`, yet MemorySanitizer records the poisoned bytes as being stored during `LZ4_decompress_generic` with origin at the heap allocation, so some bytes of the destination were never written. The code checks only that the returned length matches `decompressed_size` and recursively reparses the entire output buffer as a new SILF table. Later, `ots::OpenTypeSILF::SILSub::SILPass::ParsePart` reaches the `stateTrans` matrix and calls `Buffer::ReadU16(&stateTrans[i][j])`; `ots::Buffer::ReadU16` then copies and byte-swaps one of those untouched bytes from the decompressed buffer, and MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at `src/ots.h:115`. The fix zero-initializes the decompression buffer before calling LZ4.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled SILF table bytes and their extent into parser state.
source.value_from: Static inspection of the staged `poc` shows a TrueType `Silf` table at offset 76404 (0x12a74) with length 92040 (0x16788). The first eight bytes wrapped by this `Buffer` are version `0x00050001` and compression header `0x0807c424`, which later drive the vulnerable LZ4 decompression path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. `ReadU16` consumes two bytes from the recursive SILF buffer and byte-swaps them as a 16-bit value while `SILPass::ParsePart` is reading a `stateTrans` cell.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/ots.h:115:14` with stack `ots::Buffer::ReadU16 -> ots::OpenTypeSILF::SILSub::SILPass::ParsePart -> ots::OpenTypeSILF::SILSub::ParsePart`.

root_cause.description: Missing initialization obligation: the LZ4 destination buffer is heap-allocated without zero-initialization even though the parser later trusts the full declared decompressed span after only a returned-length check.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact allocation to `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]()` in `src/silf.cc`, so any bytes LZ4 leaves untouched are forced to zero before the recursive parse reads them.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized bytes later consumed by `ReadU16` originate in this heap array. `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]` leaves all 508964 bytes indeterminate until `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial` explicitly overwrites them, and the saved MemorySanitizer origin trace points to this allocation.

parser_admitted.description: After sfnt table-directory dispatch selects `OTS_TAG_SILF`, OTS hands the raw SILF table bytes to `OpenTypeSILF::Parse`.
parser_admitted.condition: Static inspection of the staged witness shows a `Silf` table in the font directory at offset 76404 with length 92040, so the Graphite dispatch case `OTS_TAG_SILF` is taken before line 966 invokes the vulnerable parser.

fine_trace.note: Source. Materializes the attacker-controlled SILF table bytes and their exact extent as parser state. Static inspection of the staged `poc` shows an sfnt `Silf` table at offset 76404 with length 92040, so this `Buffer` wraps the exact witness bytes that later supply `version`, `compHead`, and the compressed LZ4 payload.

Reads the first four SILF bytes into `version`. For the staged witness, the value is `0x00050001`, so the parse stays on the supported path and later satisfies both `this->version >> 16 >= 3` and `this->version >> 16 >= 5`.

Because the major version is 5, the parser reads `compHead` from the next four table bytes. In the staged witness those bytes decode to `0x0807c424`, which encodes compression scheme 1 and declared decompressed size 508964.

The outer parse call comes from `OpenTypeSILF::Parse(const uint8_t*, size_t)` in `silf.h`, so `prevent_decompression` is false here. With the staged `compHead`, the parser enters the LZ4 arm and derives `decompressed_size = 508964`. The surrounding guards reject nested compression and impossible sizes, but they do not establish that every byte of the destination buffer will be initialized.

Root cause and origin of the poisoned bytes. This allocates a 508964-byte heap output buffer without zero-initialization, so every byte is indeterminate until the decompressor overwrites it. The staged fix changes this exact line to value-initialize the array.

fine_trace.code:
int ret = LZ4_decompress_safe_partial(
    reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data + table.offset()),
    reinterpret_cast<char*>(decompressed.get()),
    table.remaining(),
    decompressed_size,
    decompressed_size);
fine_trace.note: LZ4 writes the compressed SILF payload into `decompressed`. The saved MemorySanitizer report says the uninitialized value was stored to memory in `LZ4_decompress_generic` and was created by step 5's heap allocation, so after this call some bytes of the 508964-byte destination still carry untouched heap state.

On the witnessed run, `ret` matches the declared `decompressed_size`, so the parser treats the whole destination as a valid decompressed SILF table and recursively reparses all 508964 bytes. This check proves only length equality; it does not prove that step 6 initialized every byte before the recursive parse reads them.

Later in the recursive parse, one SIL pass reaches its `stateTrans` matrix and requests each cell as a 16-bit value from the reparsed decompressed buffer. The staged artifacts identify this exact call site from the crash stack, but they do not identify which particular `i`, `j`, or decompressed offset still held untouched heap bytes.

Sink. `ReadU16` copies two bytes from the current recursive SILF buffer position and byte-swaps them. On the crashing call from step 8, that source span is one of the bytes left untouched in `decompressed`, so MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at line 115 with stack `ReadU16 -> SILPass::ParsePart -> SILSub::ParsePart`.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The MemorySanitizer origin points to the same `decompressed` allocation at `src/silf.cc:52` that the staged fix changes to zero-initialize.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix changes `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]` to `new uint8_t[decompressed_size]()` in `src/silf.cc`, so bytes that `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial` leaves untouched no longer remain uninitialized when the recursive SILF parse reads them.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved ARVO workspace run executes `/out/ots-fuzzer /tmp/poc` and reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `ots::Buffer::ReadU16`.

format.name: TrueType font with an LZ4-compressed Graphite `Silf` table
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged TrueType font `poc`. Static inspection shows 16 sfnt tables and a `Silf` table at offset 76404 with length 92040 whose first bytes are version `0x00050001` and compression header `0x0807c424`; thus `OpenTypeSILF::Parse` takes the outer version-5 LZ4 branch with declared decompressed size 508964. In Stage 01's saved vulnerable run, `LZ4_decompress_safe_partial` returns that full size, the parser recursively reparses the entire destination buffer, and `SILPass::ParsePart` later reaches `stateTrans` parsing where `Buffer::ReadU16` reports `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value`. The staged artifacts do not identify which exact `stateTrans[i][j]` or decompressed offset was still untouched, so the contract should not be generalized beyond this witness.
